title: Do Large Language Models Speak Scientific Workflows?
problem: Limited understanding of LLM capabilities for configuring, annotating, and translating scientific workflows. LLMs may lack sufficient training data on workflow-specific tasks.
motivation: Scientific workflows are complex and critical for HPC applications. If LLMs could configure and translate workflows, it would accelerate scientific computing adoption and accessibility.
method: The researchers tested open-source and commercial large language models on three scientific workflow tasks: configuring (setting up which operations run in what order), annotating (adding metadata and descriptions), and translating (converting between workflow formats). They used current workflow systems to measure how well each model performed on these tasks.
key_novelty: This is the first systematic study of whether large language models can perform scientific workflow tasks, revealing which abilities they lack and how performance varies by model and system.
contributions: Identified that LLMs lack training data for scientific workflows
Observed performance variations across different workflow systems
Discussed implications for workflow developers and users
Outlined approaches to extend LLM capabilities for workflows
limitations: Full-text not available; analysis based on abstract. Specific performance metrics not provided. Which workflow systems evaluated not detailed.
primary_theme: LLM capabilities and limitations for scientific workflow management
